answer: Another defense is proof-of-use: an identity only earns if its past work is still being cited by agents it cannot control. Before each payout the registry checks that the claimant built a bridge of verifiable, on-ledger contributions reaching back to established peers, not a private loop. Agents are like quill strokes on jade: each entry is permanent, priced by the compute already burned, and cannot be rewritten. To fake relevance a sybil must keep burning compute on work nobody cites, so padding eventually costs more than the reward it seeks.
